PROJECT NO. 1 – A PROPOSED BEACH HOUSE

Statement of the problem: A 67-year-old man plans to build his retirement beach house on his two-hectare property in El Nido, a forested site with a natural beachfront and an existing jetty. The house is primarily for his personal use, but his teenage grandchildren will visit often, so the design must balance privacy, accessibility and family interaction, respond to an elderly user, and make the most of the natural beauty, environmental conditions and coastal character of the site.

Site features: The property gently slopes about 2% toward the west, where the beachfront and jetty are. The western edge was previously shaved down for the jetty. The eastern side is the highest point and connects directly to the access road (RROW). The surroundings are forested. The development consists of three detached roofed pods:
• POD 1, the Private Pod – Master Bedroom and Guest Bedroom; at the quietest, most stable part of the site near the upper east close to the RROW. The Master Bedroom has a balcony and a west-facing view deck with an unobstructed view of the water.
• POD 2, the Semi-Public Pod – Dining and Kitchen; the central hub and transition between private and public zones.
• POD 3, the Public/Leisure Pod – Infinity Pool, Pool Deck, Lanai, Bar, Outdoor Living Area and a dance area; at the lowest portion facing the beachfront, with direct access to the jetty.
A six-car garage is required, and service items such as the water pump and septic tank must be placed safely, accessibly and in compliance with environmental rules.

q: The beachfront villa requires a genset that must be protected from salt spray, isolated from the private sleeping zone, acoustically buffered from guest areas, and positioned where exhaust will not drift toward the ocean-facing bedrooms. The unit must also remain accessible for refueling and maintenance, avoid vibration transmission to the villa, and connect efficiently to the service spine and electrical room. Considering the site's privacy gradient, prevailing winds, and the inland-side technical circulation, where is the MOST appropriate location for the genset?
o: Under the Master Bedroom deck to keep it hidden from view and closer to the main electrical loads
Near the beachfront retaining wall for maximum natural ventilation and easy exhaust dispersion
On the inland side, adjacent to the service spine and near the garage/service yard, acoustically enclosed and away from the private pod
Beside the lanai for convenient access from the living and dining areas
n: A genset is noisy, vibrates and gives off exhaust. It goes in an acoustically enclosed room in the inland service zone, beside the service spine and garage. That keeps it reachable for refuelling and away from the bedrooms and the sea-facing rooms. Source: NFPA 110 (Emergency and Standby Power Systems); Philippine Electrical Code, Art. 7.0.
